body: I'd like to nominate https://github.com/WICG/view-transitions/issues/239 for discussion, although I won't be there for the meeting.

Thank you all for attending the meeting today and a special thank you to Chris Wilson for taking meeting notes! Here are the notes from this meeting (the next one is at https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11290):

### Agenda  
Attendees: Joey Arhar, Keith Cirkel, Dan Clark, Emilio Cobos Álvarez, Mason Freed, Chris Harrelson, Olli Pettay, Simon Pieters, Noam Rosenthal, Chris Wilson, Luke Warlow, Panos Astithas  
Scribe: CWilso

1. Review past action items
    1. Keith will record the consensus in the [dialog requestClose causes several issues with regard to interplay of CloseWatcher](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11230) issue.
        1. [Done](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11230#issuecomment-2828244185).
    1. Kurt will summarize the various options around [support fragment references in the `<link>` tag's href attribute](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11019) in the issue.
        1. [Kurt](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11019#issuecomment-2842866537) and [Noam](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11019#issuecomment-2842890117) commented.
    1. Olli will find the Gecko experts to chime in on [consider changing Response's url so it includes a fragment](https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/1167). Chris will ask Domenic for a Chromium perspective.
        1. [smaug] did ask. [Domenic](https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/1167#issuecomment-2829332317) and [Valentin](https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/1167#issuecomment-2858525595) commented.
1. Carryovers from last time
    1. None.
1. New topics
    1. [Simon] [Form Submission: Fix the "Double Submit problem" at the spec level](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/5312)
        1. Consensus that this is a plausible path. Simon will create a spec PR.
    1. [Domenic/Nick] [Carry UserActivation across cross-document View Transitions](https://github.com/WICG/view-transitions/issues/239)
        1. Carryover since Domenic isn't attending today.
    1. [Noam] [Expanding the concept of internal resource links](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11286)
        1. Consensus that fragment identifiers are a plausible path. 
    1. [Luke] [Define an optional value and use it for setting dialog returnValue](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11280)
        1. Simon agrees that this is a good change to make.

### Action Items

1.  @zcorpan will create a spec PR for [Form Submission: Fix the "Double Submit problem" at the spec level](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/5312).

### Minutes  
Panos: review past action items: dialog requestClose, done: any follow ups?  
Mason: I think it reached a rough consensus. My pref is still what chrome currently does, not having a close watcher for a disconnected thing.  
Luke: consensus is the theoretical Chromium model is what we want to trend to.  My spec needs updating.    
Will do in a couple of weeks, busy next week, then we can review.  Should alleviate most current issues with dialog and request close.  
Mason: happy to review.  WPT should be up to date with those changes already, but we should check.

Panos: next action, fragment references in `<link href>`  
Dan: Kurt is on vacation this week, let's roll over.

Panos: last action, Gecko to chime in on response URL containing fragment and Chris asking for Chromium perspective.  Moving along.

Panos: new topics: form submission double submit.  
Simon: In the last comment linked, I porosed using a formal validation mechanism as the way to solve this problem.  Just checking if there's interest/concern from others.  
Joey: Your suggestion should not break websites.  Hopefully nothing should break with that.  
Mason: Is there a time limit?  If I submit and come back an hour later and submit, does it error again?  
Simon: Maybe a five second limit or something?  
Mason: just calling out the difference between accidental double-submit and intentional second submit.  
Simon: The solution to users wanting to submit again is they get a validation message and they can click again to do the submission.  
Mason: So the validation message says "click here to submit again?"  
Simon: yes.  
Luke: I'm not against the issue but I'm not sure it's a big enough issue to fix as a web platform fix; you're probably handling it on the server?  Doesn't warrant too much complexity to fix, at least.  
Mason: The only counterpoint to that is when Joey solved some of this a while back there are definitely a prevalence of sites that do nothing to fix this.  PRobably long tail sites, but still.  
Panos: sounds like a plausible solution, you're going to create a spec PR?  
Simon: yes

Panos: TOPIC:  carry useractivation across cross-document View Transitions?  (no one here to discuss, carry over) 

TOPIC:  [Expanding the concept of internal resource links](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11286)  
Noam: We talked about this briefly in the context of CSS.  Wanted to dive into one aspect, have higher level discussion, and also understand the constraints between and come up with a direction.  
Idea of using fragmented identifiers to have elements to address each other declaratively.  
 E.g. loading styles from a style element.  Or script in inline script; addressing it from another document without it having to be an external URL.  Prior art is the new linkrel aspect.  Another one is svg filter and clip path references. One constraint raised before is that in an unsupported browser we will try to load the doc from the cache from the network.  I put some other alternatives in the github issue e.g. a new URL scheme rather than fragment identifier, but there are backwards compatibility issues with non-supported browsers. Another alternative is something bespoke for script versus styles.  (e.g. script import maps).  I wanted to see the sense in the room.  
Luke: question: regarding base url changing, base element itself is reasonable to document.  Does history or nav api do something to change base url?  Having the base element broken is probably ok but not broken for nav API, that would not be ok.  A follow-up point is rather than new type attrib would just use HREF.  
Mason: same question, why not just use a separate different new attribute that says link target equals IDref.  That would get all the goodness from other attributes that are just IDrefs.  
Dan: Some of the thinking on building on prior art, should consider that developers are already sort of working with.  If it hasn't turned out to be a problem with rel=expect, I'm not super worried.  May not be best to overcomplicate adding more stuff to the platform to solve these temporary issues.  Worth looking at if we can make it work with existing capabilities.  
Simon: I remember we discussed a new attribute for rel=expect, can't remember why we decided against it.  
Noam: using a new attribute that only rels existing refs: that's one of the alternatives.  Link,script, dynamic scripts, import would all have to be aware of it.  If we go down that route, I'd prefer to have a new URL scheme rather than have another non-url thing everywhere.  
Emilio: was it considered to just special-case fragment ids like CSS?  
Noam: that's whatI was putting as alternative one, it's my favorite.  That seems like it would be most obvious to developers.  
Emilio: are there use cases for mixing base urls with frag id urls because that feels like a weird thing.  
Noam: base is more about href than it is about source. When importing base is a bit strange.  
Dan: does click state have the same effect on this?  
Olli: it changes the document uri per current spec, so I don't know if it breaks (if you go back, push state then load the next page and go back).  
Noam: it's about inconsistency when you load and do push states?  
Olli: yes; can't remember at which point we calc/compute the URI for that?  
Noam: it's when you depart or it's changed.  
Emilio: I guess we do have a precedent for something like this in SVG; not sure how well it's specified in SVG.  
Noam: it's defined to some level but those are much more complex because they're mutable.  You can link to SVG and it can change.  
Panos: seems like a plausible path forward, mild concerns but no strong objections?  
Olli: Anne brought up some of these issues.  
Noam: yep.  Good to have these minutes to discuss with Anne.  
Noam: summaryL we're recommending that the alternative of fragment identifiers is a plausible direction while taking care of timing issues and compat issues to be verified with Anne.  Frag ids with no additional attributes.  For the REL=expect case, it is no change.  Make sure link rel-expect timing issues are aligned with it. (i.e. parse the relative url every time you need to access the URL)

TOPIC: optional value for setting dialog return value.  
Luke: ambiguity in HTML spec wrt  submission and dialog where if a button has no value attribute and it's used to submit, it will not override the dialogs return value.  In FF it does override its value to be the empty string. I think this is an ask for Mozilla to fix this (chrome and webkit behave this way already).  Double checking.  
Simon: seems okay to me.  
Panos: sounds like you can move forward with this proposal.
